meta.title: Bond Ladders: Coupons, Bill Discounts and Maturity Cash
meta.heading: Bond Ladders: Coupons, Bill Discounts and Maturity Cash
meta.description: A bond ladder staggers principal maturities; coupon income and returned principal are different cash flows.
meta.cardIntro: A bond ladder staggers principal maturities; coupon income and returned principal are different cash flows. Three $10,000 par bonds paying 4% and maturing in one, two and three years return $30,000 face plus $2,400 coupons when allowed to run off.

bond-ladder.intro: Choose regular coupon bonds or discount Treasury bills, enter your prices and inspect the dated cash-flow schedule. Compare retaining proceeds with renewing the same face amount; neither outstanding face nor purchase cost is a current market valuation.
bond-ladder.answer: A bond ladder staggers principal maturities; coupon income and returned principal are different cash flows. Three $10,000 par bonds paying 4% and maturing in one, two and three years return $30,000 face plus $2,400 coupons when allowed to run off.
bond-ladder.exampleNote: Original hypothetical examples checked against independent high-precision calculations and published CMS tables. No live security quote, SSA determination or external professional review is claimed.

sections.title: What is income and what is returned capital?
paragraphs: Coupon bonds distribute contractual coupons while principal remains outstanding, then return face value at maturity. In the three-rung example, the one-, two- and three-year bonds contribute 400, 800 and 1,200 in coupons. Their 30,000 face redemption is separate.
A discounted bill has no periodic coupon in this worksheet. A 10,000-face bill bought for 9,900 realizes a 100 cash-flow gain when 10,000 is paid back. It does not earn 10,000 in interest.
sections.formula: Retained cash = coupons + principal redemptions − renewal purchases. Cash + outstanding purchase cost − initial cost = modeled realized cash-flow gain.

sections.title: What does rolling the same face amount do?
paragraphs: Coupon renewals buy the same face at par and use your chosen coupon rate and term. Coupons are retained in zero-interest cash. Bill renewals buy the same face at your chosen price, retaining the difference between redemption and the new purchase cost.

This is different from reinvesting every dollar of maturity cash or adding coupon income to new principal. A maturity exactly on the horizon is retained in cash; later maturities remain outstanding. Future renewal prices and coupons are assumptions.

sections.title: How should I compare cash and outstanding balances?
paragraphs: A runoff ladder and a rolling ladder can end with very different cash while still holding different securities. The comparison shows cash, outstanding face, outstanding purchase cost and realized cash-flow gain separately.

Cash plus outstanding purchase cost minus initial purchase cost reconciles to the worksheet’s realized cash-flow gain. It does not mark securities to market, calculate unrealized gains or establish a tax basis. Do not rank the alternatives as total-return winners from this table.

sections.title: Which dates and risks does the schedule cover?
paragraphs: All initial rungs share the entered settlement date. Coupon bonds must settle immediately after a regular coupon date; dates follow month anniversaries with month-end clamping. Bills use actual calendar-day offsets. No business-day adjustments, accrued interest or irregular coupons are modeled.

The model does not price early sales, default, calls, inflation-linked securities, taxes or fees. Bill face amounts can be fractional for arithmetic; they are not TreasuryDirect order increments or evidence an auction order can execute.

questions.question: Is this a CD ladder calculator?
questions.answer: No. Coupon bonds and discount bills have distinct cash flows here. Use the separate CD ladder for APY-based deposit scenarios.

questions.question: Does the renewal rate come from live auctions?
questions.answer: No. You supply future coupon rates or bill purchase prices. These are scenarios, not market quotes.

questions.question: What happens to a maturity exactly at the horizon?
questions.answer: It pays into retained cash without another renewal. Face amounts due later remain outstanding and are not treated as cash.

meta.title: Medicare IRMAA 2026–2027: Income Years, Tiers and Surcharges
meta.heading: Medicare IRMAA 2026–2027: Income Years, Tiers and Surcharges
meta.description: IRMAA adds income-related charges to Medicare Part B and Part D premiums.
meta.cardIntro: IRMAA adds income-related charges to Medicare Part B and Part D premiums. Under the official 2027 table, individual MAGI of $112,000 has no surcharge; $112,001 enters a bracket with $83.70 Part B and $15.40 Part D IRMAA per person per month.

irmaa.intro: Select the premium year and use income and filing status from the applicable return. This guide separates the official 2026 and 2027 brackets, usual lookback years, per-person surcharges, plan premiums and exact threshold boundaries.
irmaa.answer: IRMAA adds income-related charges to Medicare Part B and Part D premiums. Under the official 2027 table, individual MAGI of $112,000 has no surcharge; $112,001 enters a bracket with $83.70 Part B and $15.40 Part D IRMAA per person per month.
irmaa.exampleNote: Original hypothetical examples checked against independent high-precision calculations and published CMS tables. No live security quote, SSA determination or external professional review is claimed.

sections.title: Which income year belongs to each premium year?
paragraphs: The official 2026 premium-year table normally uses tax-year 2024 income; the official 2027 table normally uses tax-year 2025 income. These are different years and different threshold schedules. SSA can use an older available return or make a new determination, so follow the actual notice.
The 2027 table was published by CMS on November 17, 2026. This calculator includes that announced data alongside 2026; it does not extrapolate thresholds for later unannounced years.
sections.formula: Medicare IRMAA MAGI = AGI + tax-exempt interest. Monthly surcharge = applicable Part B adjustment + Part D adjustment for selected coverage, per covered person.

sections.title: Which MAGI definition is used for Medicare?
paragraphs: For this worksheet, Medicare IRMAA MAGI is known federal AGI plus tax-exempt interest. It is not the same as every MAGI definition used for tax credits or IRA contributions. The AGI bridge does not prepare a tax return.

A Roth conversion can interact with taxable Social Security, deductions and other tax calculations. The optional added-income scenario simply adds the MAGI change you specify to the same income-year input and applies the same premium-year table; it does not calculate an optimal conversion.

sections.title: What happens exactly at a bracket boundary?
paragraphs: For a 2027 individual, 112,000 is still in the zero-IRMAA tier. At 112,001, monthly combined Part B/D IRMAA is 99.10 per person. The yearly 1,189.20 surcharge is not an income-tax marginal rate.

Intermediate upper limits are inclusive, while the final bracket begins exactly at 500,000 individual or 750,000 joint. Filing separately while living together has a distinct schedule, with the 2027 top bracket beginning at 388,000. The complete selected table is displayed beside the calculation.

sections.title: Does a joint return mean one surcharge for the household?
paragraphs: The threshold uses the joint return, but Medicare premiums and adjustments are assessed per covered person. If both spouses have the same selected coverage, multiply the per-person adjustment by two. Different coverage, plan quotes or enrollment months require separate calculations.
Part D IRMAA is additional to the selected plan’s own premium. The entered 35 plan premium in these examples is hypothetical, not an official national plan price or quotation.

sections.title: What requires a separate official decision?
paragraphs: This worksheet uses full Part B coverage and the published income tables. Immunosuppressive-drug-only premiums, subsidies, hold-harmless protection, late penalties, Medicare Advantage reductions, actual enrollment timing and out-of-pocket medical costs are outside the calculation.

Living apart throughout the applicable tax year can change the schedule for married separate filers; SSA may require an attestation. An amended return or qualifying life-changing event can warrant a different determination. Use SSA guidance for that process; this calculator neither submits nor predicts an appeal.

questions.question: Is the 2027 standard Part B premium itself an IRMAA surcharge?
questions.answer: No. The 209.40 standard monthly premium is separate from the income adjustment. The output lists surcharge and total premium amounts distinctly.

questions.question: Does only the excess income pay IRMAA?
questions.answer: No. IRMAA is a bracket-based premium adjustment per covered person, not a marginal income-tax rate applied only to the excess income.

questions.question: Can two spouses have different total costs?
questions.answer: Yes. Different enrollment, Part D plan premiums and coverage can differ even when a joint-return income threshold applies. Run separate estimates when the same-coverage assumption does not fit.
